cards.title: Pronouns, Case Concord
rule: Definition: Pronouns, Case Concord & Gender Agreement (ተውላጠ ስማት፡ ስምምዕ ኬዝን ጾታን) refers to the grammatical rules governing the substitution of nouns with pronouns, ensuring precise coordination in case (subjective, objective, possessive), grammatical number (singular, plural), and gender (masculine, feminine, neuter).

English personal pronouns are categorized into three distinct syntactic cases: subjective ($$\text{Subject Case}$$ - *I, you, he, she, it, we, they*), objective ($$\text{Object Case}$$ - *me, you, him, her, it, us, them*), and possessive ($$\text{Possessive Case}$$ - *my/mine, your/yours, his, her/hers, its, our/ours, their/theirs*). Unlike Tigrinya, where the case of a pronoun is often marked by attaching prefixes or suffixes directly to the pronoun base, English uses entirely different word forms to signal a pronoun's grammatical role in a sentence. This leads to a common case concord error (ጌጋ ስምምዕ ኬዝ) in compound constructions. For example, Tigrinya speakers often write "The director invited Aster and I" instead of the correct "The director invited Aster and me" because they translate both subjects and objects similarly without isolating the post-verbal objective slot.

examples.text: She goes to school every day.
She go to school every day.
examples.fix: She goes to school every day.

cards.title: Notes
body: Definition: Pronouns, Case Concord & Gender Agreement (ተውላጠ ስማት፡ ስምምዕ ኬዝን ጾታን) refers to the grammatical rules governing the substitution of nouns with pronouns, ensuring precise coordination in case (subjective, objective, possessive), grammatical number (singular, plural), and gender (masculine, feminine, neuter).

English personal pronouns are categorized into three distinct syntactic cases: subjective ($$\text{Subject Case}$$ - *I, you, he, she, it, we, they*), objective ($$\text{Object Case}$$ - *me, you, him, her, it, us, them*), and possessive ($$\text{Possessive Case}$$ - *my/mine, your/yours, his, her/hers, its, our/ours, their/theirs*). Unlike Tigrinya, where the case of a pronoun is often marked by attaching prefixes or suffixes directly to the pronoun base, English uses entirely different word forms to signal a pronoun's grammatical role in a sentence. This leads to a common case concord error (ጌጋ ስምምዕ ኬዝ) in compound constructions. For example, Tigrinya speakers often write "The director invited Aster and I" instead of the correct "The director invited Aster and me" because they translate both subjects and objects similarly without isolating the post-verbal objective slot.

Gender agreement (ጾታዊ ስምምዕ) presents a major challenge for Tigrinya speakers due to structural differences in how inanimate objects are treated. In Tigrinya, there is no neuter (ጾታ ኣልቦ) pronoun equivalent to the English "it". Every noun in Tigrinya is grammatically classified as either masculine or feminine. For instance, a car ("መኪና") or the sun ("ጸሓይ") is treated as feminine, while a book ("መጽሓፍ") is masculine. When translating thoughts, Tigrinya speakers often use "he" or "she" to refer to inanimate objects in English (e.g., calling a tractor "he" or a watch "she"). In standard English, all inanimate objects must strictly take the neuter pronoun "it" ($$\text{Inanimate Object} \rightarrow \text{it}$$), except in cases of deliberate literary personification.

cards.title: Choose subject or object pronouns
cards.problem: Correct the sentence: "Between you and I, Abel and me were the only ones who finished."

steps.text: **Step 1: After a preposition use the object form.** "between" is a preposition → between you and **me**.
**Step 2: As the subject of a verb use the subject form.** "Abel and me were" → Abel and **I** were.
**Step 3: Test by removing the other person.** "me were" is wrong; "I was/were" form is right; "between I" is wrong.
**Tip:** cover "you and" or "Abel and" and say the sentence with the pronoun alone.

cards.answer: Between you and me, Abel and I were the only ones who finished.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The scholarship committee awarded the funding to Aster and ________ after reviewing our academic portfolios.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The pronoun follows the preposition 'to' and forms part of a compound prepositional object ('to Aster and [pronoun]'). This slot requires the objective case ($$\text{Preposition} + \text{Object Pronoun}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often write 'Aster and I' because 'Aster and I' is common in the subject position. This is a typical case concord trap in matriculation exams. Applying the Cover-Up Test ('awarded the funding to me') makes the correct choice clear.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
እቲ ተውላጠ ስም ድሕሪ 'to' ዝብል መስተዋድድ (preposition) ስለ ዝመጸ፡ ኣብቲ ተቐባሊ ሓሳብ (objective case) ክስራዕ ኣለዎ። 'I' (ዋና ባእታ) ኣብዚ ቦታ ክኣቱ ኣይኽእልን እዩ። ነቲ 'Aster and' ዝብል ሓረግ ብምኽዋል 'awarded the funding to me' ኢልና ክነንብቦ ከለና ቅኑዕ መልሲ 'me' (Option B) ምዃኑ ንርዳእ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The old typewriter in the headmaster's office is still functional, but ________ keys are difficult to press.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The blank modifies the noun 'keys' to show ownership. This requires the possessive adjective 'its'.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often confuse 'its' (possessive adjective) with 'it's' (contraction of 'it is' or 'it has'). Option C ('its'') is a non-existent spelling. This spelling distinction is highly tested in national exams.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ኣብዚ ቦታ ናይ ወንነት መግለጺ ቅጽል (possessive adjective) እዩ ዘድልየና። 'Its' (ናቱ/ናታ ንዘይህይወታውያን) ዝብል ቃል ብዘይ ኮማ (apostrophe) ይጸሓፍ። 'It's' ግን ሕጽር ዝበለ ናይ 'it is' ስለ ዝኾነ ኣብዚ ቦታ ኣይሰርሕን እዩ። ቅኑዕ መልሲ 'its' (Option B) እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The teacher asked Ruth and ____ to collect the books.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** "Ruth and ___" is the object of "asked".

**Step 2:** Object position needs an object pronoun: me.

**Step 3:** Test: "The teacher asked me".

**Tip:** Use subject pronouns (I, he, she, we, they, who) before a verb and object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them, whom) after verbs and prepositions. Test a compound by removing the other person.

questions.q: The scholarship committee awarded the funding to Aster and ________ after reviewing our academic portfolios.
questions.label: 1. The scholarship committee awarded the funding to Aster and _
why: The pronoun follows the preposition 'to' and forms part of a compound prepositional object ('to Aster and [pronoun]'). This slot requires the objective case ($$\text{Preposition} + \text{Object Pronoun}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: The old typewriter in the headmaster's office is still functional, but ________ keys are difficult to press.
questions.label: 2. The old typewriter in the headmaster's office is still funct
why: The blank modifies the noun 'keys' to show ownership. This requires the possessive adjective 'its'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: The candidate ________ the board selected for the position has outstanding credentials.
questions.label: 3. The candidate ________ the board selected for the position h
why: The relative pronoun refers to 'The candidate' (a person). The clause that follows has a subject-verb pattern: 'the board' (Subject) + 'selected' (Verb). This indicates the relative pronoun is acting as the object of 'selected'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Since both Almaz and her sister wanted to complete the project quickly, they did all the research ________.
questions.label: 4. Since both Almaz and her sister wanted to complete the proje
why: The subject is 'they' (plural). The corresponding plural reflexive pronoun is 'themselves' ($$\text{They} \rightarrow \text{themselves}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Although my exam preparation was thorough, ________ was far more comprehensive.
questions.label: 5. Although my exam preparation was thorough, ________ was far
why: The sentence compares 'my exam preparation' with another person's preparation. The second slot must act as a subject noun phrase meaning 'her exam preparation'. This requires a possessive pronoun ('hers') which can stand alone.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Every citizen in the country is expected to do ________ duty to protect the environment.
questions.label: 6. Every citizen in the country is expected to do ________ duty
why: The subject is 'Every citizen'. In formal, traditional English grammar, indefinite pronouns like 'everyone', 'everybody', and 'every citizen' are singular and require a singular possessive adjective ('his or her').
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: The professional painter ________ portrait won the national art award was congratulated by the community.
questions.label: 7. The professional painter ________ portrait won the national
why: The relative clause shows a possession relationship: 'portrait' belongs to 'The professional painter'. This requires the possessive relative pronoun 'whose' ($$\text{Whose} + \text{Noun}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Our English teacher is much more experienced in curriculum design than ________.
questions.label: 8. Our English teacher is much more experienced in curriculum d
why: In formal comparative constructions using 'than' or 'as', the pronoun after 'than' is the subject of an implied clause: 'than I [am]'. This requires the subjective case.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Let Aster and ________ take responsibility for organizing the graduation ceremony.
questions.label: 9. Let Aster and ________ take responsibility for organizing th
why: The verb 'let' is transitive and requires its object in the objective case: $$\text{Let} + \text{Object Pronoun} + \text{Base Verb}$$.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: The new laptop is lightweight and sleek, but ________ battery life is quite short.
questions.label: 10. The new laptop is lightweight and sleek, but ________ batter
why: We need a singular possessive adjective to modify the noun 'battery life' for the singular inanimate laptop. This requires 'its'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Between you and ____, I think the test was easy.
questions.label: 11. Between you and ____, I think the test was easy.

similar.q: Complete: The gift is for Aster and ____ (I / me).
Complete: Come with Daniel and ____ (we / us).

why: A preposition takes an object pronoun: me.
"between you and I" is a common error.
questions.tip: Use subject pronouns (I, he, she, we, they, who) before a verb and object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them, whom) after verbs and prepositions. Test a compound by removing the other person.

questions.q: Saba and ____ went to the library.
questions.label: 12. Saba and ____ went to the library.

similar.q: Complete: ____ (He / Him) and his brother play football.
Complete: My friends and ____ (we / us) study together.

why: Subject position needs a subject pronoun: I.
questions.tip: Use subject pronouns (I, he, she, we, they, who) before a verb and object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them, whom) after verbs and prepositions. Test a compound by removing the other person.

questions.q: Each student must bring ____ own dictionary.
questions.label: 13. Each student must bring ____ own dictionary.

similar.q: Complete: Everyone should do ____ best.
Complete: The company has changed ____ name.

why: "Each student" is singular, so a singular possessive is used in formal grammar.
Note: "their" is also common in modern English, but "their own's" and "theirs" are wrong here.
questions.tip: Use subject pronouns (I, he, she, we, they, who) before a verb and object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them, whom) after verbs and prepositions. Test a compound by removing the other person.

questions.q: Correct the error: "Him and his sister are coming tomorrow."
questions.label: 14. Correct the error: "Him and his sister are coming tomorrow."

similar.q: Correct: Me and Ruth are friends.
Correct: Us students need more time.

questions.answer: He and his sister are coming tomorrow.
why: The pronoun is part of the subject.
questions.tip: Use subject pronouns (I, he, she, we, they, who) before a verb and object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them, whom) after verbs and prepositions. Test a compound by removing the other person.

questions.q: The prize was given to the student ____ the judges chose.
questions.label: 15. The prize was given to the student ____ the judges chose.

similar.q: Complete: The man ____ called you is here.
Complete: The woman ____ I met was kind.

why: In the relative clause "the judges chose ___", the pronoun is the object of "chose".
questions.tip: Use subject pronouns (I, he, she, we, they, who) before a verb and object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them, whom) after verbs and prepositions. Test a compound by removing the other person.

questions.q: She is taller than ____.
questions.label: 16. She is taller than ____.

similar.q: Complete: He runs faster than ____ (she does / her does).
Complete: They are older than ____ (we are / us are).

why: In formal grammar, "than" is followed by a clause: than I am.
"I am" is the subject pronoun + verb.
(Informally "taller than me" is also used, but "I am" is safest in exams.)
questions.tip: Use subject pronouns (I, he, she, we, they, who) before a verb and object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them, whom) after verbs and prepositions. Test a compound by removing the other person.

questions.q: Read: "When Aster and her brother arrived, their aunt welcomed them warmly. She had prepared their favourite meal herself." Which pronoun is reflexive?
questions.label: 17. Read: "When Aster and her brother arrived, their aunt welcomed them warmly. She had prepared their…

similar.q: Find the object pronoun.
Who does "She" refer to?

why: A reflexive pronoun ends in -self/-selves and refers back to the subject.
"them" is an object pronoun; "their" is possessive.
questions.tip: Use subject pronouns (I, he, she, we, they, who) before a verb and object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them, whom) after verbs and prepositions. Test a compound by removing the other person.

questions.q: The students did the experiment by ____.
questions.label: 18. The students did the experiment by ____.

similar.q: Complete: I made it ____.
Complete: You (plural) should help ____.

why: "by + reflexive pronoun" means alone, without help.
questions.tip: Use subject pronouns (I, he, she, we, they, who) before a verb and object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them, whom) after verbs and prepositions. Test a compound by removing the other person.

questions.q: This bag is not mine; it is ____.
questions.label: 19. This bag is not mine; it is ____.

similar.q: Complete: The book is ____ (our).
Complete: The dog wagged ____ (it's / its) tail.

why: Possessive pronouns never take an apostrophe: hers, ours, yours, theirs, its.
questions.tip: Use subject pronouns (I, he, she, we, they, who) before a verb and object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them, whom) after verbs and prepositions. Test a compound by removing the other person.

questions.q: True or false: "Who did you invite?" is acceptable informally, but "Whom did you invite?" is the formal form.
questions.label: 20. True or false: "Who did you invite?" is acceptable informally, but "Whom did you invite?" is the…

similar.q: Formal: To ____ should I send the letter?
Subject or object: "____ wrote this?"

why: True. The pronoun is the object of "invite".
Everyday English often uses "who", so both forms exist in different registers.
questions.tip: Use subject pronouns (I, he, she, we, they, who) before a verb and object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them, whom) after verbs and prepositions. Test a compound by removing the other person.
